mainTopic: Does smell (ריחא) make food forbidden? The dispute between רב and לוי, and the new משנה on offerings brought in טומאה.
overview: This amud asks whether smell (ריחא) can make food forbidden. One view (רב) says fatty kosher meat roasted beside lean נבילה becomes אסור, because the meats flavor each other. לוי disagrees: smell is nothing (ריחא לאו מילתא), and he ruled this way in practice at the house of the ריש גלותא. A ברייתא forbidding roasting two קרבנות פסח together is first read as being about the animals getting switched. After רבי ירמיה's answer, the גמרא rereads it so that it also forbids flavor-mixing, which fits רב. רב מרי links the dispute to תנאים arguing about hot bread placed on a barrel of תרומה wine. The גמרא shows that רב can say all the תנאים agree smell matters. Practical rulings follow: bread or fish roasted with meat may not be eaten with dairy, and fish roasted with meat should not be eaten at all because of danger. Then a new משנה lists five communal offerings that may be brought in טומאה but not eaten in טומאה, unlike the פסח. The גמרא explains that the count of five excludes the חגיגה of ט"ו ניסן, and it begins answering a question about the ראש חודש goats, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fatty kosher meat roasted with lean non-kosher meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The strict opinion (רב) rules that fatty שחוטה meat roasted together with lean נבילה meat becomes forbidden, because the meats flavor each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fatty kosher meat that someone roasted together with lean non-kosher meat is forbidden. Why? Because they flavor each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: if fatty kosher meat is roasted in the same oven as lean נבילה meat, the kosher meat becomes אסור. It also gives the reason: the meats 'fatten' or flavor each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two meats do not even touch. The worry is that the aroma of the fatty kosher meat goes into the נבילה and then comes back, carrying some of the נבילה's flavor into the kosher meat. In this view, aroma can carry real taste, so it can make food forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat from a properly slaughtered (kosher) animal
Meat of an animal that died without kosher slaughter; forbidden to eat
Fatty / lean
What is the reason?
They flavor (fatten) each other

phrases.english: Fatty kosher-slaughtered meat

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁצְּלָאוֹ עִם בְּשַׂר נְבֵילָה כָּחוּשׁ — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: that one roasted together with lean non-kosher (neveilah) meat is forbidden.
phrases.notes: They are in the same oven but not touching.

phrases.english: What is the reason? They flavor each other.
phrases.notes: The fatty meat's aroma enters the lean meat and returns carrying its flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה שָׁמֵן שֶׁצְּלָאוֹ עִם בְּשַׂר נְבֵילָה כָּחוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion here; the attribution to רב appears on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aroma passing between roasting meats can forbid kosher meat: fatty שחוטה roasted with lean נבילה is אסור.

steps.title: לוי rules that smell alone does not forbid food
steps.stepSummary: לוי disagrees and permits even lean kosher meat roasted with fatty נבילה, because smell is not significant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: even lean kosher meat that someone roasted together with fatty non-kosher meat is permitted. Why? It is only a smell, and a smell is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי argues with the first opinion and permits the meat even in the 'worst' case. His reason is that smell is not a real substance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי deliberately flips the case to the harder one. Now the kosher meat is lean and absorbs readily, and the נבילה is fatty and gives off a strong aroma. Even so, he permits it, because in his view ריחא לאו מילתא היא: aroma has no legal weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
Merely a smell
Smell is not a significant thing (it does not forbid)

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether ריחא מילתא is a major issue in the laws of mixtures (איסור והיתר). It is often cited in later practical halacha.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה כָּחוּשׁ,
phrases.english: And Levi said: even lean kosher-slaughtered meat

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁצְּלָאוֹ עִם בְּשַׂר נְבֵילָה שָׁמֵן — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: that one roasted together with fatty non-kosher meat is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the case in step 1, and a 'worse' one.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is merely a smell,
and a smell is not a significant thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה כָּחוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes step 1 and holds that aroma never forbids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריחא לאו מילתא: aroma does not forbid. Kosher meat roasted beside נבילה stays permitted even in the most extreme case.

steps.title: לוי ruled this way in practice at the house of the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: לוי actually ruled leniently in a real case at the ריש גלותא's house, where a kid was roasted together with pig meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי acted on his view in the house of the ריש גלותא, with a young goat and 'another thing' (a pig).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a real-life case where לוי applied his ruling. A kid was roasted next to pig meat, and he permitted the kid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעשה shows that לוי's view was not just theory; he relied on it in practice. Pig meat is very fatty and smells strong, so this is the extreme case from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted on it / ruled in an actual case
The house of the Exilarch (leader of Babylonian Jewry)
A young goat (kid)
'Something else', a polite way of saying pig

phrases.aramaic: עָבֵיד לֵוִי עוֹבָדָא בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
phrases.english: Levi acted on this ruling in the house of the Exilarch
with a kid and 'something else' (a pig).
phrases.notes: He permitted the kid even though it was roasted together with pig meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that לוי applied the ruling from step 2 in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי permitted a kid roasted together with pig, applying ריחא לאו מילתא in practice.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule against roasting two Pesach offerings together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids roasting two קרבנות פסח together 'because of mixing'. If that means mixing of flavors, it contradicts לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'One may not roast two Pesach offerings together, because of the mixing.' Doesn't that mean a mixing of flavors? That would be a difficulty for לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא against לוי. It suggests that the 'mixing' the ברייתא worries about is a mixing of tastes, which would mean aroma matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each קרבן פסח may be eaten only by the group registered for it. If roasting two side by side is forbidden because their flavors mix, then aroma does carry taste. That would contradict לוי's claim that smell is nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Pesach offerings (קרבנות פסח)
Mixing / mixture
Is it not that...? (suggesting a reading)
Mixing of flavors

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין צוֹלִין שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד
phrases.english: They raised an objection: one may not roast two Pesach offerings together
because of the mixing.
Is it not the mixing of flavors,
and this is a difficulty for Levi!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין צוֹלִין שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד מִפְּנֵי הַתַּעֲרוֹבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks לוי's position from steps 2–3 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's rule that ריחא לאו מילתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא's 'mixing' means the flavors mix through aroma, then aroma is significant. That contradicts לוי.

steps.title: The concern is mixing up the bodies, not the flavors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is worried the two animals' bodies will be switched, not that their flavors will mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is because of mixing up the bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends לוי by rereading the ברייתא. The 'mixing' means the two roasted animals might get switched between the groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group may eat only its own פסח. If two skinned, roasted animals sit together, a group might take the wrong one. The ברייתא is about that practical mix-up, so it says nothing about aroma, and לוי is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing up of the bodies (the animals themselves)

steps.confusionAlert: תערובת גופין does not mean the meats physically blend together. It means the two whole animals might be confused, so one group ends up eating the other group's פסח.

phrases.english: No, it is because of the mixing up of the bodies.
phrases.notes: The groups might switch offerings by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'mixing' meant mixing of flavors through aroma.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's 'mixing' means the animals might be switched between groups, so it does not contradict לוי.

steps.title: Proof from 'even a kid and a lamb' that the concern is mixing up bodies
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says the rule applies even to a kid and a lamb. That makes sense only if the worry is mixing up the animals, not mixing flavors.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, since the end of the ברייתא teaches: 'even a kid and a lamb.' If you say the reason is the bodies, that explains why it says 'even a kid and a lamb.' But if you say the reason is mixing of flavors, what difference is there between a kid and a lamb and a kid and a kid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the ברייתא's own wording. The word 'even' fits only the 'mixing bodies' explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kid and a lamb look different, so 'even' teaches something new: once skinned and roasted, they can still be confused. If the concern were flavors, two different animals would be no more of a חידוש than two kids. Then the word 'even' would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, it is logical (introduces support)
The latter clause of a source
A lamb
It is understandable if you say...
What difference is there between ... and ...?

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds that aroma can forbid. לוי holds ריחא לאו מילתא and permits, even with pig. At this stage the ברייתא about two פסחים is read as worrying only about the animals being switched (תערובת גופין), as 'even a kid and a lamb' shows. Steps 7–11 revisit this: after רבי ירמיה's answer, the גמרא rereads the ברייתא so that it also forbids flavor-mixing.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the latter clause teaches: even a kid and a lamb.
Granted, if you say it is because of the bodies,
that is why it teaches 'even a kid and a lamb.'
phrases.notes: Even different-looking animals can be confused once skinned.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִפְּנֵי תַּעֲרוֹבֶת טְעָמִים,
phrases.english: But if you say it is because of the mixing of flavors,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי גְּדִי וְטָלֶה מָה לִי גְּדִי וּגְדִי.
phrases.english: what difference is there between a kid and a lamb and a kid and a kid?
phrases.notes: Under the flavor explanation, the word 'even' would teach nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 5 from the wording of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא's concern is תערובת גופין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא: 'even a kid and a lamb'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the סיפא supports reading the ברייתא as תערובת גופין, which defends לוי. This reading is temporary: step 7 uses it against רב, and steps 8–11 reread the ברייתא so that its main clause forbids תערובת טעמים.

steps.title: If only switching animals is the worry, mixed flavors must be allowed, which refutes רב
steps.stepSummary: Building on the proof in step 6, the גמרא concludes that the ברייתא forbids only תערובת גופין. That means mixed flavors are allowed, which seems to refute רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? You are forced to say that it is forbidden because the bodies might get mixed up, but a mixing of flavors is allowed. Shall we say this is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the proof from step 6 and turns it into an attack on רב. If the ברייתא only worries about switching the animals, then flavor-mixing must be fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the words 'even a kid and a lamb' showed that the ברייתא's worry is switching the animals. If that is the only worry, then roasting together and letting flavors pass between the meats is allowed. רב holds that smell and flavor passing between roasting meats does matter, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what?' This introduces a forced conclusion from what was just shown.
Perforce; you are forced to say
Mixing of bodies, meaning the two animals might be switched
Mixing of flavors between the meats
A refutation; a strong challenge that seems to knock out a view

phrases.english: Rather, what?
Perforce, because of mixing of the bodies
phrases.notes: This is the conclusion proven in step 6.

phrases.english: is it forbidden
but mixing of flavors is permitted
Shall we say this is a refutation of רב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the proof from step 6, which helped לוי, and uses it as an attack on רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that smell and flavor passing between roasting meats is significant
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא forbids only because of switching bodies, then it implies that flavor-mixing is permitted, which goes against רב.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the ברייתא speaks of roasting in two separate pots
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה defends רב. The ברייתא's case is one where the animals were roasted separately, so flavors could not mix anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he roasted them in two pots.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge to רב. He says the ברייתא is describing a case where flavors could not mix at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animals were kept apart, no flavor passed between them. So the ברייתא's ruling, which is based only on switching bodies, says nothing about whether mixed flavors are allowed. רב's view is therefore not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?' This narrows a source to a specific situation.
He roasted it
Pots

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he roasted them in two pots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a case where flavor cannot pass between the animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's case is two פסחים roasted together in one oven, where aroma would pass between them. Since it forbids only because of תערובת גופין, it implies flavor-mixing is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The meats were kept apart, so the ברייתא proves nothing about flavor-mixing.

steps.title: A קרבן פסח cannot be made in a pot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבי ירמיה's wording. A פסח must be roasted directly on fire, so 'in two pots' cannot be meant literally.
steps.simpleTranslation: In two pots? Could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact words of רבי ירמיה's answer. A פסח made in a pot would be forbidden anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the פסח to be צלי אש, roasted directly by fire. Meat made inside a pot is not fire-roasted. So the case cannot literally be 'in pots', and the answer needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Could it enter your mind?' This expresses that an idea is impossible.
Roasted directly by fire. The פסח must be made this way.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רב. It only attacks the wording of רבי ירמיה's answer, which the גמרא will repair in the next step.

phrases.english: In two pots? Could it enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: A פסח cooked in a pot is not fire-roasted, so it is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רבי ירמיה's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'in two pots' in רבי ירמיה's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח must be roasted directly on fire, so a case of pots cannot be what the ברייתא means.

steps.title: Correction: roasted in a way that is like two pots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording. The animals were roasted on fire, but separated as if each were in its own pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: like two pots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי ירמיה's answer so that it no longer describes forbidden pot-cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals are roasted directly on the fire, but they are kept apart, for example by distance or a divider. The point stays the same: no flavor passes between them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say.' This corrects the wording of a statement.
Like; similar to

phrases.english: Rather, say: like two pots.
phrases.notes: The animals are separated as if each were in its own pot, but both are roasted on the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by changing 'in two pots' to 'like two pots'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is literal pot-cooking, which is invalid for a פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animals are roasted on fire but separated, as if in two pots.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא so it fits רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now teaches two things. Mixing flavors is forbidden, and even when flavors cannot mix, it is still forbidden because the animals might be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it says: One may not roast two פסחים together because of mixing. What mixing? Mixing of flavors. And even like two pots, where there is no mixing of flavors, it is forbidden because of mixing of bodies, and even a kid and a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the whole ברייתא so that it actually supports רב. Flavor-mixing is forbidden, and there is a second reason to forbid as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא, 'because of mixing', now means mixing of flavors, which agrees with רב. The ending, 'even a kid and a lamb', now refers to the separated 'like two pots' case, where only switching bodies is a concern. This also explains the proof from step 6 without hurting רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what it is saying.' This introduces a rereading of a source.
קרבנות פסח (Paschal offerings)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can be read in a way that fits רב. Flavor-mixing is forbidden, and the ending about 'even a kid and a lamb' refers to a separated case where only switching the animals is a concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rescues רב's view that smell matters. It also shows that a single ruling in a ברייתא can rest on two different reasons in two different cases.

phrases.english: And this is what it says:
One may not roast two Paschal offerings together
because of mixing.
What mixing? Mixing of flavors.
phrases.notes: This part agrees with רב.

phrases.english: And even like two pots,
where there is no mixing of flavors
it is forbidden because of mixing of bodies,
and even a kid and a lamb.
phrases.notes: This ending now belongs to the separated case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the defense of רב by rereading the whole ברייתא using the corrected case from step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids only because of switching bodies, so flavor-mixing is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids flavor-mixing, and in the separated case it also forbids because of switching bodies.

steps.title: רב מרי: this matches a dispute among תנאים about hot bread on a barrel of תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי brings a dispute among תנאים. Is hot bread placed on top of a barrel of תרומה wine forbidden to non-כהנים because it absorbed the wine's smell?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: It is like a dispute among תנאים. One who takes hot bread out of the oven and places it on the opening of a barrel of תרומה wine: רבי מאיר forbids, and רבי יהודה permits. רבי יוסי permits wheat bread and forbids barley bread, because barley draws in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי opens a new line. He suggests that the רב and לוי argument about smell was already argued by earlier תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot bread soaks up the smell of the wine underneath it. רבי מאיר forbids the bread, as if the smell made it like תרומה. רבי יהודה permits it. רבי יוסי splits the case: barley soaks up smell strongly, while wheat does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute among תנאים
One who removes bread from the oven
Hot bread
The holy portion given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים
Draw in; absorb

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: It is like a dispute among tanna'im.
One who removes hot bread from the oven

phrases.aramaic: וּנְתָנָהּ עַל פִּי חָבִית יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה —
phrases.english: and places it on the opening of a barrel of teruma wine
Rabbi Meir forbids it,
and Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
And Rabbi Yosei permits wheat bread
and forbids barley bread,
because barley draws in the smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reread ברייתא in step 11 forbids תערובת טעמים, which now cuts against לוי. רב מרי opens a new line: the רב and לוי dispute is itself a dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread on a barrel of תרומה wine: רבי מאיר forbids, רבי יהודה permits, and רבי יוסי forbids only barley bread.

steps.title: Suggesting that the תנאים argue about whether smell matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנאים disagree over exactly the רב and לוי question: is smell significant?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not a dispute among תנאים, where one master holds smell is nothing, and the other master holds smell is something?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how רב מרי's comparison works. רבי יהודה would be like לוי, and רבי מאיר would be like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה permits the bread because he holds smell is nothing, just like לוי. רבי מאיר forbids it because he holds smell is something, just like רב. If so, רב and לוי are each following a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not?' This proposes a reading that the גמרא may later test.
Smell; aroma
Something significant
One master holds

phrases.english: Is it not a dispute among tanna'im?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: רֵיחָא — לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: One master holds that smell is nothing,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, matching לוי.

phrases.english: and one master holds that smell is something.
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, matching רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from step 12 lines up with רב and לוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the תנאים's dispute about bread on a barrel of תרומה wine really about whether smell matters?

steps.title: For לוי it is clearly a dispute among תנאים; must רב also say so?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that לוי must side with רבי יהודה. It then asks whether רב is also forced to say it is a dispute among תנאים, or whether everyone could agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to לוי, it is certainly a dispute among תנאים. According to רב, shall we say it is a dispute among תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It will check whether רב can explain רבי יהודה in a way that does not disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's prohibition can only come from smell mattering. So לוי must say the תנאים argue, and he follows רבי יהודה. For רב, there may be another option: maybe רבי יהודה permits for some other reason and also agrees that smell matters. Step 15 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
'Shall we say?' This raises a possibility for testing.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying רב is wrong. It is only asking whether רב is forced to disagree with a תנא, or whether he can fit everyone's view.

phrases.english: According to Levi, it is certainly a dispute among tanna'im.
phrases.notes: לוי holds like רבי יהודה and against רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: According to Rav, shall we say it is a dispute among tanna'im?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלֵוִי, וַדַּאי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא. לְרַב, נֵימָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 13 for לוי and opens a question about how it applies to רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can רב explain רבי יהודה's leniency in a way that does not depend on smell being insignificant?

steps.title: רב says everyone agrees smell matters
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that all the תנאים agree smell is significant. Following ריש לקיש, they only disagree about in-between cases of bread and wine barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: everyone agrees that smell is significant. Wasn't it said about that teaching, in the name of רבה בר בר חנה quoting ריש לקיש: with hot bread and an open barrel, everyone agrees it is forbidden. With cold bread and a sealed barrel, everyone agrees it is permitted. They only argued about hot bread with a closed barrel, and cold bread with an open barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. רב does not need to say this is a dispute among תנאים, because everyone agrees that smell matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש explains that the תנאים are not arguing about whether smell counts at all. They only argue about cases where it is unclear whether any smell was actually absorbed, like hot bread on a closed barrel or cold bread on an open barrel. In the clear case, hot bread on an open barrel, everyone forbids the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Smell is significant; absorbed smell counts like absorbed taste
Everyone agrees
Hot bread, which absorbs smell strongly
Cold bread, which absorbs smell weakly
A sealed or closed barrel
An open barrel

steps.confusionAlert: The dispute between the תנאים is NOT about whether smell matters. It is only about whether smell was actually absorbed in the borderline cases.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
Everyone agrees that smell is significant,
was it not stated about that teaching,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Reish Lakish:
With hot bread and an open barrel,
everyone agrees it is forbidden.
With cold bread and a sealed barrel,
everyone agrees it is permitted.
They only disagreed
about hot bread and a closed barrel,
phrases.notes: Smell might still escape through small cracks.

phrases.english: and cold bread and an open barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא רֵיחָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's question of whether רב must depend on a dispute among תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must רב's view depend on one side of a dispute among תנאים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Everyone agrees smell is significant. The תנאים only argue about borderline cases where it is unclear whether smell was absorbed.

steps.title: Two roasted פסחים are like the strongest case
steps.stepSummary: The case of two פסחים roasted in one oven is like hot bread on an open barrel, so everyone agrees smell is a problem there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this case is also like hot bread with an open barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies ריש לקיש's rule to our case of two פסחים roasted together. It is the clear case, so everyone agrees it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat roasting in an open oven is hot, and nothing blocks the smell. That matches hot bread on an open barrel, where everyone forbids. So רב's view fits every תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is similar or comparable
And this case also

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, all agree smell matters. Two פסחים roasted openly together is the strongest case, like hot bread on an open barrel.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא נָמֵי כְּפַת חַמָּה וְחָבִית פְּתוּחָה דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: And this case is also like hot bread and an open barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נָמֵי כְּפַת חַמָּה וְחָבִית פְּתוּחָה דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 15 to the case of the two פסחים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's view does not depend on a dispute among תנאים. Two roasted פסחים are the clear, forbidden case.

steps.title: Bread baked with roasting meat may not be eaten with dairy
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches that bread baked in an oven together with roasting meat may not be eaten with כותח, a dairy dip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא, son of רב חיננא the Elder, taught: bread that was baked together with roasting meat in the oven may not be eaten with כותח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical teaching based on the idea that smell matters. Bread that absorbed meat smell is treated like meat when it comes to dairy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the bread took in the meat's smell, eating it with a dairy food would be like eating meat with milk. This follows the view that smell is significant.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasted meat
Oven
כותח, a Babylonian dip made with milk

phrases.english: Rav Kahana taught,
the son of Rav Chinnana the Elder:
Bread that one baked with roasting meat in the oven,
it is forbidden to eat it with kutach.
phrases.notes: כותח contains milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִינָּנָא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from theory to a practical application of 'smell matters'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread baked with roasting meat absorbs its smell and may not be eaten with dairy.

steps.title: Fish roasted with meat may not be eaten with dairy
steps.stepSummary: רבא of פרזיקיא forbade eating a fish that was roasted with meat together with כותח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a fish that was roasted together with meat. רבא of פרזיקיא forbade eating it with כותח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that matches the previous teaching. Fish that absorbed meat flavor was treated like meat when eaten with dairy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the bread in step 17, the fish took in the meat's flavor. So eating it with a milk dip was forbidden as meat with milk.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of fish
Was roasted
Meat

phrases.english: A certain fish that was roasted together with meat,
Rava of Parzikiya forbade it
to be eaten with kutach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical case that follows the same principle as step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish roasted with meat may not be eaten with dairy.

steps.title: Even with salt it is forbidden, because of danger
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the fish may not be eaten even with salt, because fish and meat together is a health danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: it is forbidden even with salt, because it is bad for smell and for 'something else'.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי adds a stricter rule. The fish is forbidden even without dairy, for health reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new reason, not about meat and milk. חז"ל considered meat and fish together dangerous. It causes bad breath and 'something else', meaning צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt
Harmful for odor (causes bad breath)
'Something else', a polite way of saying צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: This ban is NOT about בשר בחלב. It is a separate health danger from eating meat and fish together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice of not eating meat and fish together.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Even with salt it is also forbidden,
because it is harmful for odor and for 'something else'.
phrases.notes: 'Something else' refers to צרעת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּמִילְחָא נָמֵי אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter rule to the case in step 18 for a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish roasted with meat may not be eaten even with salt, because of danger.

steps.title: Five offerings brought in impurity but not eaten in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists five communal offerings that may be brought when the people are טמא, but may not be eaten in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Five things may be brought in טומאה but are not eaten in טומאה: the עומר, the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים, the communal שלמים, and the goats of ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five communal offerings that may be offered in טומאה, but whose meat or bread may not then be eaten in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings have a fixed time, so they may be brought even when most of the people or כהנים are טמא. Being allowed to offer them does not mean they may be eaten in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Are offered in a state of impurity
The barley offering brought on ט"ז ניסן
The two wheat loaves of שבועות
The showbread on the שולחן
The goat חטאות of ראש חודש

steps.confusionAlert: 'Brought in טומאה' means it may be offered on the מזבח despite impurity. It does NOT mean it may be eaten in impurity. That is exactly what the משנה denies.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Five things are brought in impurity,
but they are not eaten in impurity:
the omer, and the two loaves,
and the showbread,
and the communal peace-offerings,
and the goats of the New Moons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These five communal offerings may be offered in טומאה but may not be eaten in טומאה.

steps.title: The פסח brought in impurity is eaten in impurity
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the five, a קרבן פסח offered in טומאה may also be eaten in טומאה, because its whole purpose is eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסח that is brought in טומאה is eaten in טומאה, because from the start it is brought only to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the exception. The קרבן פסח is different from the five offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For other offerings, the main מצוה is offering on the מזבח, and eating is secondary. The פסח exists for eating, so if offering in טומאה is allowed, eating in טומאה must be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח
From its very beginning or purpose
For eating

steps.whatToRemember: Five communal offerings: offered in טומאה, not eaten in טומאה. פסח: offered and eaten in טומאה, because eating is its main purpose.

phrases.english: The Paschal offering that is brought in impurity
is eaten in impurity,
since from the start it comes only for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the פסח with the five offerings in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח offered in טומאה may be eaten in טומאה, because its purpose is eating.

steps.title: What does the number five exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה states the number 'five' and what it comes to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Five.' What does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a question about the exact count. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A number in a משנה usually signals that something similar is left off the list on purpose. The גמרא wants to know which offering that is.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה
To exclude what?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
'Five.' To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering is the number 'five' meant to exclude?

steps.title: It excludes the חגיגה of the fifteenth
steps.stepSummary: The count of five excludes the חגיגה brought on ט"ו ניסן, which may not be offered in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the חגיגה of the fifteenth of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The number five tells us that the חגיגה of ט"ו ניסן is NOT on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought the חגיגה, a holiday offering for the whole nation, also overrides טומאה. The count of five teaches that it does not, so it may not be offered in טומאה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiday שלמים offering brought on ט"ו ניסן

phrases.english: To exclude the Festival offering of the fifteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number five excludes the חגיגה of ט"ו ניסן, which is not brought in טומאה.

steps.title: Why we might have thought the חגיגה overrides טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the mistaken idea that the משנה's 'five' comes to block. Since the חגיגה looks like a communal offering with a fixed date, one might think it overrides טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is a communal offering and it has a fixed time, it should push aside טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the משנה had to bother excluding the חגיגה. It spells out the mistaken idea that someone could have had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings with a fixed time (קרבן ציבור שקבוע לו זמן) are brought even when the people are טמא. The חגיגה is brought by everyone together on the same day, and it has a set date. So it seems to fit that rule. That is the הוה אמינא.

keyTerms.meaning: It could have entered your mind to say (introduces a mistaken assumption)
A communal offering
It has a fixed, set time
It should override (push aside) ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The חגיגה is not truly a communal offering. Each person brings his own. It only looks communal because everyone brings it at the same time, and that is exactly why someone might mistakenly have grouped it with true communal offerings.

phrases.english: For it could have entered your mind to say:
phrases.notes: Introduces the הוה אמינא.

phrases.english: since it is a communal offering,
phrases.notes: Everyone brings it together on the festival.

phrases.english: and it has a fixed time,
phrases.notes: It is tied to ט"ו ניסן.

phrases.english: it should override ritual impurity.
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken conclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 23's answer by stating the mistaken assumption that the exclusion comes to reject.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion is needed because one might think the חגיגה, as a quasi-communal offering with a fixed time, overrides טומאה.

steps.title: Make-up days mean no overriding שבת, so no overriding טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that since the חגיגה can be made up all seven days, it does not override שבת. Since it does not override שבת, it does not override טומאה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: since it can be made up during all seven days, it does not push aside שבת. And since it does not push aside שבת, it does not push aside טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason the חגיגה cannot be brought in טומאה. It finishes the answer to 'what does five leave out'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering only pushes aside a prohibition when it truly must happen on that exact day. The חגיגה has תשלומין, meaning it can be brought later in the festival, so it is not urgent enough to override שבת. The גמרא then links the two rules: whatever does not override שבת also does not override טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the real lesson, rejecting the mistaken idea)
Make-up opportunity, a later chance to bring it
All seven days of the festival
It does not override שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Five offerings were listed in order to exclude the חגיגה of ט"ו. It has תשלומין all seven days, so it does not override שבת, and therefore it does not override טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general link. Whether an offering overrides טומאה follows whether it overrides שבת, and that depends on whether its date is truly fixed with no make-up.

phrases.english: it teaches us:
phrases.notes: Now comes the real rule.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כׇּל שִׁבְעָה —
phrases.english: since it has make-up time all seven days,
phrases.notes: It can still be brought later in the festival.

phrases.english: it does not override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: It is not urgent enough to push aside שבת.

phrases.english: and since it does not override Shabbat,
it does not override ritual impurity.
phrases.notes: Final ruling on the חגיגה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הוה אמינא of step 24 and gives the real reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the חגיגה has תשלומין all seven days, it does not override שבת, and therefore it does not override טומאה.

steps.title: Why not also list the festival goats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not also list the goats brought as sin-offerings on the festivals, which are also brought in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה also list the goats of the festivals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list as incomplete. The festival goats (שעירי הרגלים) are communal offerings with a fixed time, so why are they missing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'five' as if the list were complete. But שעירי הרגלים also fit the rule: they are communal, fixed in time, and brought in טומאה. Leaving them out seems to make the count wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it also teach (a challenge that something is missing)
The goats brought as sin-offerings on the festivals

phrases.english: Let it also teach
phrases.notes: Challenge formula.

phrases.english: the goats of the festivals!
phrases.notes: These are also communal offerings brought in טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained what 'five' excludes, the גמרא now asks whether the list leaves out something that should be included.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שעירי הרגלים meet the same criteria as the listed offerings, so the count of five seems incomplete.

steps.title: The festival goats are already included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the festival goats are already covered by the משנה's phrase זבחי שלמי צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It already taught them under 'the communal peace-offering sacrifices.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משנה. The festival goats are not missing; they are hidden inside one of the five items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase זבחי שלמי צבור is read as covering more than just the communal שלמים. One way to understand this is that the word 'זבחי' refers to the festival goats, while 'שלמי צבור' refers to the שבועות lambs. So the list of five already includes them.

keyTerms.meaning: It already taught it
The communal peace-offering sacrifices (one of the five in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The festival goats are actually חטאות, not שלמים. They are included here because of how the משנה's phrase is read (the word 'זבחי'), not because they belong to the שלמים category.

phrases.english: It already taught it:
phrases.notes: Rejects the claim that something is missing.

phrases.english: the communal peace-offering sacrifices.
phrases.notes: According to רש"י, 'זבחי' covers the festival goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording to include the missing item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The festival goats are missing from the list of five.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are included within the phrase זבחי שלמי צבור.

steps.title: Then why list the ראש חודש goats separately?
steps.stepSummary: If זבחי שלמי צבור includes goats, then the ראש חודש goats should not need their own listing either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the goats of ראש חודש should also not be listed, since it already taught 'the communal peace-offering sacrifices'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer into a new problem. If goats are already included in זבחי שלמי צבור, why does the משנה list שעירי ראשי חדשים as a separate item?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer said the general phrase covers festival goats. By the same logic it should also cover the ראש חודש goats. Yet the משנה lists them separately, which makes that listing look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (turning the previous answer into a problem)
The goats brought as sin-offerings on ראש חודש

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Builds on the previous answer.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים נָמֵי לָא נִיתְנֵי,
phrases.english: the goats of the New Moons should also not be taught,
phrases.notes: The משנה does list them explicitly.

phrases.english: since it already taught the communal peace-offering sacrifices!
phrases.notes: That phrase should already cover them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים נָמֵי לָא נִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 27 by applying its logic to the ראש חודש goats.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that זבחי שלמי צבור includes goats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the general phrase includes goats, then listing שעירי ראשי חדשים separately is redundant.

steps.title: The גמרא begins its answer
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אמרי' opens the גמרא's answer to why the ראש חודש goats are listed separately. The answer itself continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is about to answer the question about the ראש חודש goats, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אמרי' introduces an answer given in the name of the sages of the study hall. No content is given yet. The learner should expect an explanation of what makes the ראש חודש goats different enough to need their own mention.

phrases.english: Say in answer:
phrases.notes: The answer continues in the next section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the response to the קשיא of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup only; the resolution follows on the next amud
